claim: Let \(X=L_p(\mu)\) be an infinite-dimensional real \(L_p\) space, let \(2\le p<\infty\), and let \(r,s\in(0,1]\). For the finite-set parametric property \((r,s)\)-\(\mathrm{SQ}_{<\aleph_0}\), if \(p=2\) then \(X\) has the property exactly when \(r^2+s^2\le1\). If \(p>2\), then \(X\) has the property exactly when either \(r^p+s^p<1\), or \(r^p+s^p=1\) and \(X\) has no weak unit in its Banach-lattice order. Equivalently, at the critical boundary for \(p>2\), the property holds exactly when every positive element of \(L_p(\mu)\) has a nonzero lattice-disjoint positive element.
integrity: The classification is proved analytically from the scalar Clarkson inequality, disjoint supports in infinite-dimensional Lp spaces, Hilbert orthogonality, and the intrinsic weak-unit criterion. No finite experiment is used as proof.
limitations: Real infinite-dimensional \(L_p\) spaces only, with \(2\le p<\infty\).
No classification is asserted for finite-dimensional \(L_p\), \(1\le p<2\), complex scalars, or general Banach lattices.
The literature comparison cannot exclude an equivalent theorem under substantially different terminology or in unindexed sources.
title: Exact parametric square boundary for \(L_p\) spaces via weak units
